court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Family Court in Matrimonial Suit No. 272 of 2018
case_name: Km. Ankita Devi vs Shri Jagdependra Singh @ Kanhaiya
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which was dismissed by the trial court. The husband challenged this order and it was dismissed. The wife then filed an amendment application to delete Section 12 of the Act and incorporate Section 11 instead. This was allowed by the trial court. The husband again challenged this order but it was dismissed. The matter was directed to be proceeded exparte against the husband, who absented himself.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized without performance of Saptapadi (Sat Fera) is not valid.
legal_principles.held: It was pointed out that the ceremony of Saptapadi (Sat Fera) was not performed and no marriage ceremony had taken place, therefore, the marriage was not valid.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for annulling a marriage under Section 12 of the Act must be filed within one year after knowledge of the alleged fraud.
legal_principles.held: In paragraph 23 of the written statement, it has been categorically stated that as the petition under Section 12 of the Act should have been filed within a year after the knowledge of the alleged fraud, which is not available in the present case.

outcome.final_order: The final court order is not specified in the excerpt.

keywords: Latin maxim: Falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
responding to an amendment application in a matrimonial suit
arguing illegality of a court order dismissing a petition
